top_signals.title: The Military Strategic Drivers Behind China’s Nuclear Expansion
top_signals.summary:
In June 1993, a group of Second Artillery Corps senior leaders gathered at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. The organizers brought Li Xuge, recently retired commander of the Second Artillery, as a special guest for the event. Li had watched the Second Artillery develop from its infancy to this day, when China finally tested a ballistic missile capable of striking anywhere within the United States. However, Li had received significant pushback on the program in the years prior to this launch.  In the early 1990s, China’s military strategy was shifting to focus on war with Taiwan. top_signals.title: Sabbagh: Space Security Requirements Have Surged
top_signals.summary:
UAE-based AI-powered space tech firm Space42 reported net income for the third quarter of $31.1 million, up sharply from a year ago. Revenue climbed over 6% to just under 145 million dollars, powered by the launch of its Thuraya-4 satellite and surging government demand. Karim Michel Sabbagh, Managing Director of Space42 spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on Horizons Middle East & Africa on the numbers.
 (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
top_signals.summary: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.
